items.claim: The nitrogen oxides component was rate-based for certain coal-fired units and did not add a cap or allowance trading.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The nitrogen oxides component was rate-based for certain coal-fired units, began in 1996 and did not introduce a cap or allowance trading.
items.sourceEvidence: “The nitrogen oxides component was rate-based for certain coal-fired units” and “did not introduce a cap or allowance trading”
items.usefulness: Shows how the program treated the pollutants differently.

items.claim: Sulfur dioxide phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants; substitution or compensating units brought the total to 445 units.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Its phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants; substitution or compensating units brought the phase I total to 445 units.
items.sourceEvidence: “phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants; substitution or compensating units brought the phase I total to 445 units”
items.usefulness: Adds a concrete account of how coverage expanded.
items.qualification: Units and plants are different counts.

items.claim: Sulfur dioxide phase II began in 2000, and the final cap in 2010 was 8.95 million tons.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Phase II began in 2000. The final 2010 cap was 8.95 million tons.
items.sourceEvidence: “Phase II began in 2000. The final 2010 cap was 8.95 million tons.”
items.usefulness: Carries the sulfur dioxide timeline through its later cap.
items.qualification: The cap is not a reported actual-emissions total.

uncertainties: The synthesis says a cap is a permitted total rather than reported actual emissions; the source text does not state actual emissions.
Do not treat units and plants as interchangeable counts.
endpoint: Conclude with the contrast between the sulfur dioxide cap-and-trading mechanism and the rate-based nitrogen oxides component, noting their different timelines.
